key_insight: A lightweight structure-only predictor, calibrated with conformal risk control, can decide when MLIP predictions are trustworthy enough to skip DFT while guaranteeing bounded residual error.
engineering_relevance: This enables faster automated materials screening by reducing expensive DFT labeling calls without sacrificing a user-defined error-risk target.
method: Map atomic numbers and Cartesian coordinates to a fixed geometric descriptor.
Predict MLIP-DFT disagreement in energy, average force, and maximum force with a lightweight model.
Use conformal risk control to set a DFT-selection threshold that controls the expected error of retained MLIP labels at level α.
evidence_signal: Across eight dataset-MLIP pairs, the method met the same risk guarantee while sending 7% and 14% fewer configurations to DFT than committee baselines at α=0.3.
watch_item: Performance depends on calibration and can shrink when committee methods already capture the same errors, especially when DFT labels and MLIP training data use the same functional and basis set.
paper_title: Risk-Controlled DFT Selection for Machine-Learned Interatomic Potentials
